subject: MAP: Performance & Quantization Benchmarks for Acme Inference Pilot
messages:
From: Taylor Burns <taylor@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP and benchmarking for Acme inference pilot

Marissa —

Thanks for the call earlier. We're excited to move the pilot to the evaluation phase. To keep procurement moving we need a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a short, reproducible benchmarking plan so our infra team can validate latency/throughput under our workload. High-level asks from Acme:

- End-to-end latency targets (p50/p95), TTFT for chat flows, and sustained throughput at 64/128 token contexts.
- Concurrency behavior: 1, 8, 32, 64 simultaneous sessions.
- Quantization comparison: BF16/FP16 baseline vs INT8 and INT4, including model quality regression checks (ROUGE/F1 on our sample eval set).
- Kernel profile summary (bottlenecks per NVidia A100 / T4) if available.
- Proposed close timeline: pilot evaluation complete by end of March (we need a go/no-go).

Can you put these into the MAP and include a clear evaluation plan and files we can run? Also include any caveats about TTFT vs steady-state throughput.

Best,
Taylor
Taylor Burns
Senior ML Platform Lead, Acme Analytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Burns <taylor@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmeanalytics.com>, dev_patel@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: MAP: Performance & Quantization Benchmarks for Acme Inference Pilot

Taylor / Samir —

Thanks — attached is a draft MAP and runnable benchmark plan (see attachments). High-level summary below; the PDF has the timeline, responsibilities, and sign-off checkpoints. The CSV contains the actual harness commands and sample datasets for reproducibility.

Summary (high level):
- Goal: Validate that Redwood Dedicated instance meets latency and throughput SLOs for the pilot workload while measuring quality drift under quantized execution.
- Evaluation windows: 
  - Week 1 (Mar 1 - Mar 5): Baseline profiling (BF16/FP16) — TTFT, p50/p95, throughput at 1/8/32/64 concurrency.
  - Week 2 (Mar 8 - Mar 12): INT8 quantization trials + kernel profiling; automated regression checks on Acme eval set.
  - Week 3 (Mar 15 - Mar 19): INT4 experiments (conservative rollout), additional regression windows, and canary runs against production-like traffic.
- Close timeline: Decision checkpoint scheduled with procurement and platform on Friday Mar 26. Final go/no-go expected Mar 27.

Key measurement definitions included in the plan:
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): measured from request accept to first token emitted by the model (median & 95th).
- E2E latency: request to last-token; reported as p50/p95 with token-count buckets (32/64/128).
- Sustained throughput: tokens/sec measured over 60s windows under target concurrency.
- Quality regression checks: document uses ROUGE-L and task-specific F1 from your sample set; threshold for acceptable drift is 1.5% absolute for critical tasks.

Attachments: MAP_Acme_Inference_Pilot_v1.pdf, benchmark-plan.csv (contains harness commands, model versions, and seed prompt sets).

I'll loop in Dev for kernel/quant details — Jon and Dev will help run the INT8/INT4 passes and provide kernel-level profiles so you can see hot kernels and memory patterns.

Next step: Can your infra team run the baseline harness Mar 1-5? We can provide a dedicated queue on Redwood Dedicated and a short runbook.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: Performance & Quantization Benchmarks for Acme Inference Pilot

Marissa / Jonas —

Quick tech note / plan for the benchmark harness (details attached as kernel-profile-20260223.tar.gz stub):

1) Baseline configs we will exercise:
   - Model: open-llm-v2-13B (baseline FP16/BF16), variants: q8_0 (INT8), q4_1 (INT4) using Redwood quant pipeline.
   - Hardware: A100-40GB (primary), fallback T4 for cost profile.
   - Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8; Seq lengths: 32, 64, 128.
   - Concurrency: 1 / 8 / 32 / 64 simulated sessions (continuous stream for throughput tests).

2) Kernel profiling approach:
   - Use nvprof / Nsight sampling during the steady-state phase (after warmup 60s) and aggregate top-10 kernels by time and memory transfers.
   - Record KV cache hits, attention kernel time, softmax/backprop-like ops (inference-only kernel names vary by compiled operator).

3) Quantization & regression checks:
   - INT8: run warm-up then 3 repeated eval passes across Acme's eval set; compute ROUGE-L and task F1 per pass, report mean/std.
   - INT4: run only after INT8 passes; if mean F1 degradation > 1.5% vs BF16 baseline on critical tasks, flag and stop further rollout.
   - Regression harness stores per-example outputs and a diff index for quick triage.

4) TTFT caveat: TTFT is highly sensitive to our continuous batching heuristics and KV cache priming. We'll provide the exact config we use (max_batch_delay_ms, prefix_cache enabled) — CSV in the plan.

Attachments: kernel-profile-20260223.tar.gz (contains a README, example nvprof snippets, and trace summaries).

I'll instrument the harness to produce a machine-readable summary (CSV) with p50/p95 TTFT, p50/p95 E2E, tokens/sec, and per-kernel time percentage.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Taylor Burns <taylor@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acmeanalytics.com>, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: Performance & Quantization Benchmarks for Acme Inference Pilot

Marissa / Dev —

This looks good. Acme infra can run baseline Mar 1-5; we'll use a small fleet of A100 nodes and mirror your harness. Two quick clarifications before we start:

1) For concurrency tests, should we use per-session KV caching (stateful chat) or stateless single-turn calls? Our key use is multi-turn chat — want the numbers to reflect per-session KV reuse.
2) For the regression rule: is the 1.5% absolute F1 drop applied per-task or aggregated across the eval set? We have two high-priority tasks; if one degrades by 2% and the other improves by 0.5% the aggregate might be OK but one task is critical.

Thanks — once we have these answered we'll kick off.

Best,
Taylor

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Burns <taylor@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Final MAP & bench results summary (baseline + quant trials) — next steps to close

Taylor / Samir / Team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Below is the consolidated summary from the baseline run (Mar 1-5) and our quantization passes (Mar 8-19). Full CSVs and the regression PDF are in the Drive link. Key points and next steps for the MAP sign-off:

Baseline (BF16 / FP16) — A100-40GB, per-session KV cache enabled:
- TTFT (32 tokens output): p50 = 36ms, p95 = 98ms.
- E2E latency (64 tokens): p50 = 145ms, p95 = 380ms.
- Sustained throughput (64 concurrent sessions): 1,920 tokens/sec aggregate (30 tokens/sec per session average after warmup).
- Kernel hotspots: attention kernel (34% time), kv-serialize (18%), softmax/normalization (12%). Detailed kernel breakdown attached.

INT8 (q8_0) trials:
- TTFT delta vs BF16: +8ms median, p95 +22ms.
- E2E latency change: median +9%, p95 +12%.
- Throughput: aggregate improvement ~18% at 64 concurrency due to smaller memory bandwidth pressure.
- Quality: ROUGE-L mean delta = -0.9% (within 1.5% threshold) for Task A; Task B delta = -1.3% (within threshold).

INT4 (q4_1) conservative trials:
- TTFT delta vs BF16: +24ms median, p95 +60ms.
- E2E latency change: median +27%, p95 +35%.
- Throughput: aggregate improvement ~35% at high concurrency but higher variance across sequences.
- Quality: Task A delta = -2.7% (exceeds 1.5% threshold), Task B delta = -0.8%.
- Action: We recommend INT4 only for non-critical background batches or with a forced human-in-the-loop for Task A. We flagged per-example diffs and attached quant-regression-report-INT4-20260301.pdf.

Regression checks and triage:
- For any model/quant variant we store per-example diffs and a small triage set of 250 examples that fail the threshold. The harness produces a diff index so customers can quickly inspect failures.
- We ran three repeated passes per quant variant and reported mean/std; INT4 showed higher variance indicating potential instability at tail lengths.

MAP next steps and close timeline:
- Mar 3: Acme infra ingests harness and confirms baseline reproduction (you said you would run Mar 1-5 — please confirm reproduction status).
- Mar 12: Redwood provides full kernel profile and a trimmed recommendations doc (quant knobs, batch_delay_ms, cache hints).
- Mar 19: Joint canary: run a 2-hour production-like traffic window with INT8 enabled on 5–10% of traffic.
- Mar 26: Procurement + platform decision meeting (go/no-go).

Links / artifacts: Drive: https://drive.company.com/drive/folders/1AqzAcmeBenchResults, HubSpot: https://hubspot.company/contacts/ACME-1234

If this looks good, I'll update the MAP PDF (attached) with the INT8 recommendation and the INT4 caveats and send for signoff.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

P.S. Dev attached the kernel traces — @Dev, if you want to add any final notes on the attention kernel optimization opportunities, please reply and I'll update the doc before we send to procurement.
